messages:
maya: FYI I'm seeing progressive GPU memory growth on canary after the kernel-picker change at 10:12. Usage drifts up ~200MB per 1k requests and never drops. Suspect fragmentation or leaked buffers.

jonah: Can you paste the exact repro and which node?

maya: canary-3 (a100-80GB). repro: `./dev/repro/gpu_mem_buildup.sh --model redwood/13b --batch 4 --seq 1024 --iters 500 --picker fast-kernel`

maya: quick nvidia-smi snapshot during run:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 12.2 |
| GPU  Name        Temp  Pwr:Usage/Cap  MemUsage | GPU-0  A100-SXM4  37C  200W/400W  42.1GiB / 80.00GiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

sandeep: output of `torch.cuda.memory_summary()` after ~300 iters? Also profiler snapshot from perf-bot if available.

maya: pasted trimmed memory_summary (after 300 iters):
```
Allocated tensors: 21 (total 40.3 GiB)
Cached memory:  6.8 GiB
Current active allocations: 7.2 GiB
Largest allocation: 12.0 GiB
```

maya: perf-bot uploaded a profiler clip: s3://redwood-perf/captures/1759876543/kernel-picker-canary-clip.pb

perf-bot: nightly profiler capture for canary-3 (1759876500) available: top ops: matmul_fast (42%), matmul_stable (38%), kv_cache_update (8%). Trace contains repeated 64MiB workspace allocations.

rachel: repeated workspace allocations smell like allocator churn. Did we enable per-invocation workspace sizing in the new kernel path?

jonah: I inspected kernel-picker diff — it toggles between `matmul_fast` and `matmul_stable` based on seq len heuristics. The fast path calls `alloc_workspace(curr_batch, seq)` for each forward and frees after. The old path reused a global workspace per-device.

sandeep: sounds like we regressed buffer reuse. Two hypotheses: 1) true leak (forgot free) 2) fragmentation due to multiple small allocs preventing large contiguous chunk for KV. We should run our fragmap tool: `python tools/fragmap.py --pid <pid> --gpu 0 --interval 5 --duration 600`

maya: ran fragmap for 10 minutes. Output (summarized):
```
free chunks: 124
largest free chunk: 6.1GiB
total free: 37.9GiB
# allocations > 32MiB: 310
external fragmentation score: 0.47
```

maya: largest free chunk is only 6.1GiB which explains occasional OOM for 12GiB KV snapshot loads. But total free ~38GiB indicates not a leak.

jonah: good find. So this is fragmentation. Any recent change in allocation granularity?

rachel: kernel-picker created a per-request vector of small workspaces (powers-of-two sizes for each micro-batch) and freed them. That pattern causes many >32MiB but <512MiB chunks. GC/defrag of allocator not triggered.

sandeep: mitigations: a) switch back to global reusable workspace per-device b) introduce size-bucket coalescing in allocator c) pre-reserve large contiguous buffers for KV ops to avoid split allocations.

maya: quick test: I forced reuse by setting env REDWOOD_FORCE_GLOBAL_WS=1 and re-ran repro for 1k iters. Memory stabilized, external fragmentation score dropped to 0.12, and no progressive growth.

jonah: thanks. Can we get a minimal patch to make kernel-picker prefer the reusable workspace for the fast path? If yes, do a canary rollback in config.

rachel: I'll open a small PR to prefer device-global workspace with a flag in kernel picker. Also adding unit test that simulates repeated micro-batch allocations and asserts fragmentation score <0.2.

maya: created a short reproducer script for CI: `tests/repro/test_frag_kernel_picker.py` that runs in CI with a small emulated allocator. Pushes to my branch.

perf-bot: created perf issue #1428 with attached fragmap and profiler clip.

jonah: next steps: 1) rachel PR to revert to reuse + test; 2) sandeep to prototype allocator bucket coalescing; 3) maya to run canary with PR. If all green, promote to dedicated cluster.

maya: one more note — KV cache hot paths still request large contiguous allocations (12GiB) when sequence length spikes. We should add fallback to split into multiple KV chunks before OOM and log that path in the console for ops to see.

rachel: agreed. Adding split-and-log behavior behind feature flag `kv.split_on_oom=true` in the canary rollout plan.

jonah: thanks all. This looks like fragmentation not a leak. Good catch on the kernel-picker change. :thumbsup:

sandeep: I'll start a follow-up RFC on allocator bucket strategy next week.

maya: leaving logs & fragmap exports in the thread s3: s3://redwood-debug/1759876543/

jonah: closing the loop — please add a note to the rollout doc and tag me when canary passes.

maya: will do.
